# Changelog {#sec-changelog .unnumbered}

## v1.0.7

[On CRAN since 2026-10-30.]{.text-muted}

**Changes that affect results**

* **AR confidence set on the whole real line.** `AR_test()` and `ivDiag()` now find the Anderson-Rubin confidence set exactly. With one instrument, the set solves a quadratic inequality, so it is an interval, two rays, the whole line, or empty. With several instruments, the whole line is scanned and each boundary is refined by root finding. Earlier versions inverted the test only within 10 SEs of the 2SLS estimate and could miss part of the set, for example reporting `[0.0642, Inf)` instead of `(-Inf, -1.1605] Union [0.0640, Inf)`. The AR test of zero effect (`Fstat`) is unchanged.
* **`ltz()` with `weights`.** The adjustment term now uses weighted cross-products, consistent with the weighted 2SLS fit. With one instrument, it equals one over the weighted first-stage coefficient. In the example in @sec-sensitivity, the LTZ estimate changes from 3.6088 (SE 0.8112) to 3.7441 (SE 0.7568). Results without weights are unchanged. (#18, thanks [\@Rok-Novak](https://github.com/Rok-Novak))
* **`tF()` with a very weak first stage.** Below an *F* of 4, where the table of @lee2022valid starts, `tF()` now returns an infinite critical value and an interval that covers the whole real line. Earlier versions used 18.66, the value at *F* = 4, for any smaller *F*, so the interval was too narrow. `plot_coef()` labels such an interval "Unbounded CI".
* **Reproducible bootstrap.** Each bootstrap draw gets its own random-number stream derived from `seed` (through **doRNG**), so results are the same with or without parallel computing and for any number of cores. Up to v1.0.6, `seed` did not reach the parallel workers, so the default parallel bootstrap changed from run to run. For a given `seed`, bootstrap results differ from those of v1.0.6.

**New features**

* **Fuzzy RD designs.** `ivDiag()` gains `running`, `cutoff`, `rd.poly`, `bandwidth` and `kernel`. The instrument is the indicator for crossing the cutoff, and a polynomial in the running variable, separate on each side, is partialled out, so only the jump at the cutoff identifies the effect. With several cutoffs, each unit is compared with its nearest cutoff. See @sec-rd.
* **New dataset `mcclendon`** [@mcclendon2014], a randomized encouragement design, now the main example in this manual and in the help pages.
* **This manual is now a Quarto book** in `tutorial/`, with raw-data figures, a weak-instrument AR example, and a chapter on fuzzy RD designs. `rueda` is still shipped.

**Bug fixes**

* The parallel bootstrap in `ivDiag()` works again. After a GitHub change in July 2024, the worker cluster was stopped twice and the call failed with "invalid connection". The cluster is now stopped once on exit, also after an error, and the sequential backend is restored. CRAN v1.0.6 was not affected. (#12, thanks [\@kjohnsen](https://github.com/kjohnsen))
* Harmless "NaNs produced" warnings from `felm()` in bootstrap resamples are silenced.

**Other changes**

* The bootstrap workers start with `parallelly::makeClusterPSOCK()`. **future** is no longer imported. (#15, thanks [\@HenrikBengtsson](https://github.com/HenrikBengtsson))
* `ivDiag()` no longer calls `set.seed()`, so the caller's random-number state is left as it was.
* DESCRIPTION gives the GitHub address for bug reports (#8, thanks [\@olivroy](https://github.com/olivroy); #16, thanks [\@HenrikBengtsson](https://github.com/HenrikBengtsson)) and cites @lal2023trust by DOI.
* The help pages of the datasets give their Dataverse sources and licenses.
* Unit tests added (`tests/testthat`). Unused imports (**fixest**, **glue**) removed.
